J 2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home appearing for the learned Additional Advocate General for the respondents and perused the record.
3.
The case of the petitioner was that the detenu was an employee of Panchayat Raj department, due to disputes with his wife he gave up his job and came to Hyderabad.
He married another woman, by name, Sujatha.
In search of his livelihood, he started working as a Sales Executive in a Herbal Online Company.
In the year 2021, he and his wife were implicated in a false case in Crime No.102 of 2021 by Meerpet Police, alleging that he was running prostitution business.
He was released on bail.
For no fault of him, again he was roped in another case in Crime No.318 of 2021 of L.B. Nagar Police Station, remanded to judicial custody and was released on bail.

Strangely on 24-4-2021, the 2nd respondent served the impugned order of detention and admitted the detenu in Central Prison,
Charlapalli.
4. He further submitted that a charge sheet was also filed in Crime No.102 of 2021 on 25-2-2021.
Charge sheet was yet to be PNR,J & Dr.GRR,J filed in Crime No.318 of 2021.
The aforementioned two cases were pending for adjudication.
The respondent police wantedly detained him even though they had opportunity to file for cancellation of bails.
The trial courts had granted conditional bails to the detenu.
The detaining authority had not considered the conditions granted in the bail order.
The detention order was passed in a mechanical way.
Until the guilt of detenu was proved, it could not be presumed that he would fall within the purview of causing damage or insecurity to the public at large.
There was no material to justify the allegation that he was an immoral traffic offender.
Except the cases referred in the order of detention, no other cases were registered against him in any of the police stations and prayed to order for release of the detenue.

5. A counter affidavit was filed by the 2nd respondent justifying the detention order stating that the detenu indulged in immoral trafficking by procuring innocent girls from West Bengal, A.P. and other parts of the State under the guise of providing livelihood and forcibly dragging them into prostitution and living on the earnings of prostitution.
As such, it necessitated the respondent PNR,J & Dr.GRR,J to pass the order of detention against the detenu with a view to prevent him from further committing such offences.
He submitted that he exercised his power in tune with the provisions of the Act and passed the order of detention.
The order of detention did not suffer from any legal infirmities and prayed to dismiss the writ petition.

sentences.text: Perused the detention order and the consequential confirmation order.
The detaining authority had taken into consideration two offences for passing the order of detention against the detenu.
The two cases are pertaining to immoral trafficking and running organized prostitution business with girls.

(1) Crime No.102 of 2021 registered under Section 370(A)(2) IPC and Sections 3, 4, 5 and 7 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 by Meerpet Police and (2) Crime No.318 of 2021 registered under Section 370(A) IPC and Sections 3(1)(2)(a), 4, 5(1)(a) and 7 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention)
Act, 1956
by L.B. Nagar Police
. The detenu was arrested in Crime No.102 of 2021 by Meerpet Police on 8-2-2021 and produced before the court on the same date.
He was released on bail 17-2-2021.
Soon after his release from jail in the above case, he PNR,J & Dr.GRR,J was again involved in a similar case vide Crime No.318 of 2021 of L.B. Nagar Police Station.

7. The detaining authority after considering that he was granted bail in both the cases but continued to involve in trafficking women/girls even while on bail and was living on the earnings of the prostitution and that there was imminent possibility of his being indulged in similar prejudicial activities again which would be detrimental for maintenance of public order, passed the order of detention.
Thus, he considered the bail orders before passing the order of detention.
No conditions were imposed by the concerned judges while releasing the detenu on bail in both the crimes.

Thus,
the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the detaining authority had not considered the conditions granted in the bail order is devoid of merit.
8. In the matter of preventive detention, the law is clear that as far as subjective satisfaction is concerned, it should be reflected in detention order.

Once the detaining authority is subjectively satisfied about the detenu habitually involving in similar offences and difficult to control him under normal circumstances, he is free PNR,J & Dr.GRR,J to pass an appropriate order under Section 3 of the Act 1 of 1986 by fulfilling the conditions stated therein.
No infirmity was found in the reasoning of detaining authority or the procedure followed by him.
Hence it is considered fit to dismiss the petition.
9. In the result, the writ petition is dismissed.
No costs.

Miscellaneous petitions pending, if any,
shall stand closed.

_ P. NAVEEN RAO, J _____________________ Dr. G. RADHA RANI,
